reference_use.conclusion: The snapshot (project d8d46c95, Mathlib 25730c7c) contains the frozen Ch06 contract. Submission is byte-identical to it, and no `slicing_im_coarea_*` name exists in the project or in the 369 DAG nodes. SimonGMT supplies the needed area-formula library: weighted_area_formula_lipschitzOn_fiberSum, injective_area_formula_lipschitzOn, area_image_criticalSet_eq_zero, euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn, a Whitney extension (source only, no .olean), Lusin, the upper density theorem, the linear co-area formula and HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt with uniqueness. subproblem.title: Weighted approximate tangent planes on a C¹ antilipschitz chart image (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2), proof of 1.6 and Remark 1.8(1))
subproblem.statement: Let Q, n ∈ ℕ, V ⊆ ℝ^Q open, M ⊆ V Hⁿ-null-measurable, θ : ℝ^Q → ℝ with θ > 0 on M and θ Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ V, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open and Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q of class C¹ such that c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω and some c > 0. Then for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M ∩ Φ(Ω) (a.e. for Hⁿ restricted to M ∩ Φ(Ω)) and every w ∈ Ω with Φ(w) = y, the subspace range DΦ(w) is a weighted approximate tangent space of (M, θ) at y, i.e. HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y (range DΦ(w)).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (Q n : ℕ) (V M : Set (Eucl Q)) (θ : Eucl Q → ℝ) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl Q) (Ω : Set (Eucl n)), IsOpen V → M ⊆ V → NullMeasurableSet M (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q)) → (∀ y ∈ M, 0 < θ y) → (∀ K : Set (Eucl Q), IsCompact K → K ⊆ V → IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ K) (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q))) → IsOpen Ω → ContDiff ℝ 1 Φ → (∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ w ∈ Ω, ∀ w' ∈ Ω, c * ‖w - w'‖ ≤ ‖Φ w - Φ w'‖) → ∀ᵐ y ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q)).restrict (M ∩ Φ '' Ω)), ∀ w ∈ Ω, Φ w = y → HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ Φ w).toLinearMap)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^Q = Eucl Q with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|. Hⁿ = μHE[n] is Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure: on ℝⁿ it equals Lebesgue measure Lⁿ = volume, it is invariant under isometries and translations, and it scales by λⁿ under x ↦ λx. A map Φ is c-antilipschitz on Ω if c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.
Setting. V ⊆ ℝ^Q is open, M ⊆ V is Hⁿ-null-measurable, θ > 0 on M, and θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ V. Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q is C¹, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ is open, and Φ is c-antilipschitz on Ω (c > 0). Put N := Φ(Ω). Recall η_{y,λ}(z) := λ⁻¹(z − y) (`blowUpMap y λ`). HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y T means: dim T = n and for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q), ∫_{η_{y,λ}(M)} φ(z) θ(y + λz) dHⁿ(z) → θ(y) ∫_T φ dHⁿ as λ ↓ 0.
Source. Simon Ch. 3, Definitions 1.4/1.7, the proof of Theorem 1.6 “⇒” and Remark 1.8(1) (printed arguments, specialized to one C¹ chart). This is the reviewed proof of the identically stated lipschitz-pushforward node lpf_weighted_tangent_on_c1_chart. Several of its steps are comparator-accepted DAG lemmas that a decomposition of this node may reuse with identical types: lpf_wtc_blowup_setIntegral_image (0(d)), lpf_wtc_chart_image_measurable_locally_finite (0(b),(c)), lpf_wtc_lusin_compact_pieces (step 1), lpf_wtc_ae_zero_density_off_set (0(f)), lpf_wtc_tangent_transfer (step 2), lpf_wtc_density_bound_of_tangent, and lpf_wtc_wtt_blowup_integral_split / lpf_wtc_wtt_remainder_vanishes (step 4).
If n > Q then Hⁿ ≡ 0 on ℝ^Q (`hausdorffMeasure_of_dimH_lt`), every Hⁿ-a.e. statement is trivial, and there is nothing to prove. Assume n ≤ Q.

0. (Preliminaries on the chart.)
 (a) For w ∈ Ω and s ∈ ℝⁿ: w + ts ∈ Ω for small t, and |Φ(w+ts) − Φ(w)| ≥ c|t||s|. Dividing by |t| and letting t → 0 gives |DΦ(w)s| ≥ c|s|. So DΦ(w) is injective and T_w := DΦ(w)(ℝⁿ) = LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ Φ w) has dimension n. Φ is injective on Ω; for y ∈ N let w_y ∈ Ω be the unique point with Φ(w_y) = y, and T_y := T_{w_y}. The Lean conclusion “∀ w ∈ Ω, Φ w = y → …” concerns exactly w = w_y.
 (b) Ψ := (Φ|Ω)⁻¹ : N → Ω is (1/c)-Lipschitz. N is σ-compact (Ω is a countable union of compact sets and Φ is continuous), hence Borel, and M ∩ N is Hⁿ-null-measurable.
 (c) N is locally Hⁿ-finite. If K ⊆ ℝ^Q is compact, then Ψ(N ∩ K) has diameter ≤ diam(K)/c, so it lies in a closed ball B̄ ⊆ ℝⁿ. Φ is Lipschitz on B̄ (C¹ on a compact convex set), say with constant Λ, so Hⁿ(N ∩ K) ≤ Λⁿ Lⁿ(B̄) < ∞.
 (d) (Change of variables under blow-ups.) η_{y,λ} is a similarity of ratio λ⁻¹. So for every set S and every g ≥ 0 or Hⁿ⌞S-integrable g: ∫_{η_{y,λ}(S)} g dHⁿ = λ^{−n} ∫_S g∘η_{y,λ} dHⁿ (translation invariance and μHE[n](λS) = λⁿ μHE[n](S), Mathlib `euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀`).
 (e) (C¹ blow-up of N; Simon: “since x ∈ N_j and N_j is a C¹ submanifold, lim ∫_{η(N_j)} f = ∫_{T N_j} f”.) Claim: for every y ∈ N and φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q), lim_{λ↓0} ∫_{η_{y,λ}(N)} φ dHⁿ = ∫_{T_y} φ dHⁿ.
 Proof. Let spt φ ⊆ B_R(0) and w := w_y.
 - By (d) and the injective area formula for Φ on Ω (Φ is injective, and Lipschitz on bounded subsets of Ω; Simon Ch. 2 (3.2)/(3.5), SimonGMT `injective_area_formula_lipschitzOn` and its weighted fibre-sum form `weighted_area_formula_lipschitzOn_fiberSum`), the integral equals λ^{−n} ∫_Ω φ((Φ(v) − y)/λ) JΦ(v) dv, where JΦ(v) := √det(DΦ(v)*DΦ(v)).
 - The substitution v = w + λs turns it into I_λ := ∫ 1_{(Ω−w)/λ}(s) φ((Φ(w+λs) − Φ(w))/λ) JΦ(w+λs) ds.
 - If the integrand is nonzero, then w, w + λs ∈ Ω and |Φ(w+λs) − Φ(w)| < λR, so c|λs| < λR, i.e. |s| < R/c. For λ ≤ 1 the integrand is therefore bounded by sup|φ| · max_{|z−w| ≤ R/c} JΦ(z) and vanishes for |s| ≥ R/c.
 - For fixed s, as λ ↓ 0: w + λs ∈ Ω eventually (Ω open), (Φ(w+λs) − Φ(w))/λ → DΦ(w)s, and JΦ(w+λs) → JΦ(w).
 - By dominated convergence I_λ → ∫_{ℝⁿ} φ(DΦ(w)s) JΦ(w) ds = ∫_{T_y} φ dHⁿ. The last equality is the linear area formula for the injective linear map DΦ(w) (Simon Ch. 2 (3.1); Mathlib `LinearMap.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image`, normDet).
 For nonnegative φ ≥ 1_{B_R(0)} this also shows sup_{0<λ≤1} λ^{−n} Hⁿ(N ∩ B_{λR}(y)) < ∞.
 (f) (Upper Density Theorem, Simon Ch. 1, 3.6; SimonGMT `Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_6`, or the accepted DAG lemma lpf_wtc_ae_zero_density_off_set.) If μ is a Borel regular measure on ℝ^Q and A is μ-measurable with μ(A) < ∞, then for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ ℝ^Q ∖ A, lim_{ρ↓0} ρ^{−n} μ(A ∩ B_ρ(y)) = 0. Finite Borel measures on ℝ^Q, and Hⁿ restricted to sets of finite measure, are Borel regular.

1. (Compact pieces with continuous weight — Remark 1.8(1).) Let V_1 ⊆ V_2 ⊆ ⋯ be open sets with compact closures closure V_i ⊆ V_{i+1} ⊆ V and ⋃_i V_i = V. Fix i.
 - ν_i(B) := ∫_{B ∩ M ∩ V_i} θ dHⁿ defines a finite Borel measure (∫_{M ∩ closure V_i} θ < ∞). θ is ν_i-measurable, being a.e. strongly measurable on M ∩ closure V_i by `IntegrableOn`.
 - Choose a Borel M_i′ ⊆ M ∩ V_i with Hⁿ((M ∩ V_i) ∖ M_i′) = 0.
 - For each j ≥ 1, Lusin's theorem for the finite Borel measure ν_i (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17; SimonGMT `Chapter01.Lusin`) gives a closed F with ν_i(ℝ^Q ∖ F) < 1/(2j) and θ|F continuous. Inner regularity gives a compact C_{i,j} ⊆ M_i′ ∩ F with ν_i((M_i′ ∩ F) ∖ C_{i,j}) < 1/(2j). Thus C_{i,j} ⊆ M ∩ V_i is compact, θ|C_{i,j} is continuous, and ν_i((M ∩ V_i) ∖ C_{i,j}) < 1/j.
 - Hence ν_i((M ∩ V_i) ∖ ⋃_j C_{i,j}) = 0, and since θ > 0 on M, also Hⁿ((M ∩ V_i) ∖ ⋃_j C_{i,j}) = 0.
 As M = ⋃_i (M ∩ V_i), it suffices to prove: for each fixed C := C_{i,j}, the conclusion holds at Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ C ∩ N. Note that θ ≥ m_C := min_C θ > 0 on C (a continuous positive function on a compact set), so Hⁿ(C) ≤ m_C^{−1} ∫_C θ dHⁿ < ∞.

2. (Unweighted tangent plane of C on the chart — proof of 1.6 “⇒”.) Two exceptional sets, by 0(f):
 (i) With μ := Hⁿ⌞C (finite) and A := C ∖ N: for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ C ∩ N, ρ^{−n} Hⁿ((C ∖ N) ∩ B_ρ(y)) → 0.
 (ii) For each of the countably many rational balls B ⊆ ℝ^Q, with μ := Hⁿ⌞(N ∩ B) (finite by 0(c)) and A := (N ∩ B) ∖ C: for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ C ∩ B, ρ^{−n} Hⁿ((N ∖ C) ∩ B ∩ B_ρ(y)) → 0. Since B_ρ(y) ⊆ B for small ρ when y ∈ B, and the rational balls cover ℝ^Q, this gives: for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ C ∩ N, ρ^{−n} Hⁿ((N ∖ C) ∩ B_ρ(y)) → 0.
 Let y ∈ C ∩ N satisfy (i) and (ii), and let φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q) with spt φ ⊆ B_R(0). Using 0(d),
 ∫_{η_{y,λ}(C)} φ = ∫_{η_{y,λ}(N)} φ − ∫_{η_{y,λ}(N ∖ C)} φ + ∫_{η_{y,λ}(C ∖ N)} φ.
 - |∫_{η_{y,λ}(N∖C)} φ| ≤ sup|φ| λ^{−n} Hⁿ((N ∖ C) ∩ B_{λR}(y)) → 0.
 - |∫_{η_{y,λ}(C∖N)} φ| ≤ sup|φ| λ^{−n} Hⁿ((C ∖ N) ∩ B_{λR}(y)) → 0.
 - The first term tends to ∫_{T_y} φ by 0(e).
 Hence lim_{λ↓0} ∫_{η_{y,λ}(C)} φ dHⁿ = ∫_{T_y} φ dHⁿ for every φ; the exceptional set does not depend on φ. Moreover λ^{−n} Hⁿ(C ∩ B_{λR}(y)) ≤ λ^{−n} Hⁿ(N ∩ B_{λR}(y)) + λ^{−n} Hⁿ((C ∖ N) ∩ B_{λR}(y)) stays bounded as λ ↓ 0, by 0(e) and (i).

3. (Exceptional set for the rest of M.) By 0(f) with μ := ν_i and A := (M ∩ V_i) ∖ C (ν_i(A) < ∞): for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ C, ρ^{−n} ∫_{((M ∩ V_i) ∖ C) ∩ B_ρ(y)} θ dHⁿ → 0.

4. (Weighted blow-up — Remark 1.8(1).) Let y ∈ C ∩ N satisfy the conclusions of steps 2 and 3. Let φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q) with spt φ ⊆ B_R(0), and let λ > 0 be so small that closure B_{λR}(y) ⊆ V_i (possible since y ∈ C ⊆ V_i, which is open).
 - z ↦ φ(z)θ(y + λz) is Hⁿ-integrable on η_{y,λ}(M): it vanishes unless y + λz ∈ M ∩ B_{λR}(y), and by 0(d) its absolute integral is ≤ sup|φ| λ^{−n} ∫_{M ∩ closure B_{λR}(y)} θ < ∞.
 - By 0(d), ∫_{η_{y,λ}(M)} φ(z) θ(y+λz) dHⁿ(z) = λ^{−n} ∫_M φ((x−y)/λ) θ(x) dHⁿ(x) = I₁ + I₂ + I₃.
 - I₁ := θ(y) λ^{−n} ∫_C φ((x−y)/λ) dHⁿ(x) = θ(y) ∫_{η_{y,λ}(C)} φ dHⁿ → θ(y) ∫_{T_y} φ dHⁿ (step 2).
 - I₂ := λ^{−n} ∫_{C ∩ B_{λR}(y)} φ((x−y)/λ)(θ(x) − θ(y)) dHⁿ(x). Then |I₂| ≤ sup|φ| · sup_{C ∩ B_{λR}(y)} |θ − θ(y)| · λ^{−n} Hⁿ(C ∩ B_{λR}(y)) → 0, because θ|C is continuous at y and the density ratio is bounded (step 2).
 - I₃ := λ^{−n} ∫_{(M ∖ C) ∩ B_{λR}(y)} φ((x−y)/λ) θ(x) dHⁿ(x). Since (M ∖ C) ∩ B_{λR}(y) = ((M ∩ V_i) ∖ C) ∩ B_{λR}(y), |I₃| ≤ sup|φ| λ^{−n} ∫_{((M∩V_i)∖C) ∩ B_{λR}(y)} θ dHⁿ → 0 (step 3).
 Hence the weighted blow-up integrals converge to θ(y) ∫_{T_y} φ dHⁿ for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q). Together with dim T_y = n (0(a)), this is HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y T_y with T_y = LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ Φ w_y).

5. (Conclusion.) The set of y ∈ M ∩ N where the conclusion fails is contained in ⋃_i ((M ∩ V_i) ∖ ⋃_j C_{i,j}) ∪ ⋃_{i,j} (the exceptional subsets of C_{i,j} ∩ N from steps 2–3), a countable union of Hⁿ-null sets. Since M ∩ N is Hⁿ-null-measurable (0(b)), this is exactly the statement “∀ᵐ y ∂ Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ Φ(Ω)), ∀ w ∈ Ω, Φ w = y → HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y (range DΦ(w))”. ∎
 For n = 0 all steps hold verbatim: ℝ⁰ is a point, H⁰ = μHE[0] = μH[0] is counting measure, λ⁰ = 1, N is a single point or empty, and T_y = {0}.
proof_key_steps: Chart facts: DΦ(w) injective with |DΦ(w)s| ≥ c|s|; Φ(Ω) σ-compact and locally Hⁿ-finite; blow-up change of variables.
C¹ blow-up: by the injective area formula and dominated convergence, blow-ups of Φ(Ω) at y = Φ(w) converge to Hⁿ restricted to DΦ(w)(ℝⁿ).
Lusin (Remark 1.8(1)): M ∩ V_i is covered up to null sets by compact C with θ|C continuous.
Upper density theorem: Hⁿ⌞(C∖Φ(Ω)), Hⁿ⌞(Φ(Ω)∖C) and θHⁿ⌞(M∖C) have zero n-density at a.e. point of C ∩ Φ(Ω).
Weighted blow-up = θ(y)·(blow-up of C) + continuity error + zero-density remainder → θ(y)∫_{T_y} φ.

audit.reason: The prose includes the exact local integrability, positivity and chart hypotheses. Chart blow-up convergence, compact continuous-weight pieces and zero-density estimates prove the weighted tangent limit outside one null exceptional set. Injectivity gives the universally quantified preimage conclusion.
